note: Original description, based on 3 alates only (taken at light). The genus was originally Eutermes and the species is now placed in Ekphysotermes. The text was extracted by OCR from the Internet Archive scan; a few figures in the measurements were broken up by the OCR and are kept as far as they are legible.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (Placed in the genus Eutermes in the original.) Body dark chestnut brown above, pale yellowish white below. Head upright, broad, rounded behind, deeply concave in front; compound eyes very large, circular, protruding at the sides; ocelli very large, convex, oblique, close to the inner margin of the compound eye, white; the fontanelle forms a pale yellow median longitudinal stripe; postclypeus more than twice as wide as long, pale yellow, rounded at the sides and in front, flat anteriorly, divided by a pale median suture; anteclypeus white, rounded, prolonged forwards in the middle; labrum broad, rounded; mandibles large, the left with a very long and pointed apical tooth, a blunter and shorter tooth a little above the middle, and a broader and more prominent basal region, the right with a broader and less prominent basal region; antennae 16-segmented, very long and slender, pale yellow, segment 1 much longer and wider than segment 2, segment 3 very short and shorter than segments 2 and 4, segment 5 slightly longer than segment 2, segments 6 and 7 about as long as segment 5, from segment 8 lengthening progressively, segments 13—16 twice as long as wide, the last segment rounded at the apex; pronotum very broad, dark brown, the lateral margins, a very fine median line and a round spot on each side of the median line (just behind the anterior margin) paler, the margins with very long hairs, the anterior margin slightly concave, the anterior corners broadly rounded, the sides strongly narrowed towards the base, the sides and posterior margin together almost semicircular; mesothorax and metathorax rather flattened, partly pale; wings broad and rounded, the two thick anterior veins meeting at the apex, the media running in the upper part of the wing and giving off an unbranched branch near the middle, the cubitus with 6—8 very thick oblique veins; in the hind wing the media appears unbranched to the apex and the cubitus gives off at most 10 very thick oblique veins, the venation very variable; legs moderate, the femora rather thick; abdomen broad, rounded, with 9 broad dark brown chitinous tergites; cerci thick. Measurements: body length with wings 10 mm, body length without wings 5.2 mm, head length 0.97 mm, head width 1.03 mm, pronotum length 0.57 mm, width 1.0 mm, forewing length 8.4 mm, width 2.4 mm, hind wing length 7.4 mm, abdomen width 1.37 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Closely related to E. tumuli Froggatt, but much smaller and paler; the pronotum of similar shape but much smaller; the ocelli the largest of all Australian species (diameter 0.19 mm); altogether much paler than E. tumuli. Type locality: Oscar Range, Kimberley district, north-western Australia; described from only 3 alates taken at light at night, the soldier and worker unseen.
